author: Clif Droke
title: Stocks took another beating on Monday as the selling pressur
text:
Stocks took another beating on Monday as the selling pressure from last Friday’s session spilled over into the new week. The S&P 500 (SPX) sank 4.10% and is now down over 6% in the last two trading sessions. Wall Street sentiment has done an about-face in just the last few days as traders now wonder if a new bear market is arriving. As I’ll discuss in this commentary, however, the stock market’s technical profile still supports a bullish conclusion to the first major sell-off in over a year. 
Let’s begin with a rundown of the market’s latest activity. Setting the bearish tone on Monday was a sector downgrade issued by Morgan Stanley. An equity strategist for the firm, Michael Wilson, recommended that investors take profits on technology sector stocks. The tech sector was downgraded by Morgan Stanley to equal weight from overweight based on earnings revisions. 
Underscoring his bearishness on the sector, Morgan Stanley's Wilson wrote that technology “looks downright awful” as he singled out the poor performance of the semiconductors due to downward earnings revisions, as well as the “poor sell thru” of Apple Inc.’s ( AAPL ) new iPhone. Given that the market was already in a weakened internal condition as discuss in previous reports, the lack of confidence the Morgan Stanley report inspired in the market was unsurprising. 
Keeping in mind that the market is most vulnerable to negative news when there is a high degree of internal weakness, the broad market is still susceptible to bad news in the very immediate term. The stock market’s lack of near-term internal health in the last two weeks has been clearly reflected in the extraordinarily high amount of stocks making new 52-week lows on the NYSE. For instance, there were 454 new lows on Monday against only 15 new highs, which is an unacceptably negative high-low differential.
